headings.title: Overview of Hospital Bed Accessories
headings.content: Hospital bed accessories are specialized attachments and devices designed to modify standard hospital beds to meet specific therapeutic needs. These tools help maintain correct anatomical alignment, prevent complications of immobility, and enhance patient comfort during prolonged bed rest. In Nigerian healthcare facilities, where resource constraints sometimes limit the availability of advanced motorized beds, these manual accessories play a vital role in nursing care. Nurses must evaluate each patient's clinical condition to select the appropriate accessory. Improper selection or placement can lead to skin breakdown, musculoskeletal strain, or accidental injury.

headings.title: Bed Cradles and Pressure Relief
headings.content:
A bed cradle is a semi-cylindrical metal or plastic frame placed over a patient's body on the mattress. Its main function is to keep the weight of heavy bed linens off the lower extremities. 

- **Burn patients**: Protects sensitive healing skin from friction and pressure.
- **Fracture cases**: Prevents blankets from displacing traction equipment or misaligning limbs.
- **Peripheral neuropathy**: Eliminates irritation caused by sheet contact on hypersensitive feet.

When positioning a bed cradle, the nurse must ensure it is stable and does not obstruct the patient's movement or nursing procedures.

headings.title: Air Rings and Pressure Ulcer Prevention
headings.content: An air ring, often called a donut cushion, is a circular inflatable device placed under the buttocks to relieve pressure on the sacral region. However, modern nursing practice discourages the routine use of traditional ring cushions because they can actually restrict blood flow to surrounding tissues and worsen pressure ulcers. When air rings are used, they must be inflated moderately—never overly firm—and the patient must still be turned regularly. Nurses should prioritize frequent repositioning and high-specification foam mattresses over rubber air rings for effective pressure injury prevention.

headings.title: Supportive Devices: Backrests, Footboards, and Bed Blocks
headings.content:
Various supportive accessories help maintain posture and prevent secondary deformities during prolonged bed rest.

- **Backrests**: Provide an inclined surface to support patients in a sitting or semi-Fowler's position for eating or breathing ease.
- **Footboards**: Placed vertically at the foot of the bed to maintain dorsiflexion and prevent foot drop in immobilized patients.
- **Bed Blocks**: Wooden or rubber blocks placed under the bed legs to elevate either the head or the foot of the entire bed for specific treatments.

headings.title: Safety Protocols and Maintenance
headings.content: Safety remains paramount when incorporating any accessory into a hospital bed. Nurses must check that all metallic and plastic frames are free from cracks, sharp edges, or rust that could injure frail skin or tear linen. Regular cleaning and disinfection prevent cross-infection between patients. Equipment should be stored properly when not in use to avoid cluttering hospital floors, which could cause falls for staff and visitors. Any damaged accessory must be tagged out of service immediately and reported to the maintenance department.
